title: Software Engineer
description: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. KLA's Central Engineering organization is made up of nine Centers of Excellence (CoEs) spanning disciplines like automation, motion control, sensors, platform design, and packaging. Each CoE contributes not only technical deliverables but also deep expertise, best practices, and advanced tools that elevate both what we build—and how we build it. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. KLA is a global leader in process control and yield management solutions for the electronics and semiconductor industries. For decades, KLA has worked at the leading edge of deep science , taking on complex technical challenges that often take years to solve. By combining expertise in optics, sensors, machine learning, data analytics, and software engineering, KLA helps enable the ideas and devices that transform the future of technology. At KLA, innovation is driven by a belief that precision matters at the smallest scale —from nanometer‑level measurement to world‑class manufacturing quality. Our solutions support advanced manufacturing across wafers, integrated circuits, packaging, and printed circuit boards, making everyday technologies such as smartphones, data centers, autonomous systems, and connected devices possible. KLA fosters an engineering‑driven culture that values rigorous testing, continuous improvement, and collaboration across global teams. Software Quality Engineers at KLA contribute to products with real‑world impact while growing their careers in an environment that encourages curiosity, ownership, and long‑term technical excellence. The ICOS Division at KLA focuses on advanced optical inspection and metrology solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, with strong emphasis on component inspection, wafer safety, and high‑precision optical systems . ICOS products play a critical role in ensuring manufacturing quality, yield, and reliability for leading semiconductor customers. ICOS products operate at the intersection of optics, mechanics, electronics, and software , making them inherently complex and quality‑sensitive. The division’s success depends not only on innovation in inspection capability, but also on robust system validation, safe operation, and predictable software behavior across diverse customer environments . Job Responsibilities Test Automation Engineer Understand the system and customer workflows end-to-end by analyzing product requirements, architecture, and real customer use cases; translate these into automation strategy and test coverage for web applications and web services. Participate early in the SDLC by reviewing functional/system requirements and designs to ensure testability , identify risks, and define measurable acceptance criteria aligned with user journeys and service/API contracts. Build and maintain a scalable test automation framework using Playwright (web UI automation) with strong engineering practices (reusable utilities, page/component patterns, stable selectors, test data strategy, reporting). Automate critical user flows (smoke, regression, and high-risk business paths) by modeling realistic user behavior and validating the complete workflow across UI, backend services, and data stores. Develop automated validations for Web Services / APIs (service-level functional checks, contract validation, negative testing, error handling) and integrate them with UI flows for true end-to-end quality coverage. Apply AI-assisted automation practices to improve reliability and maintenance efficiency (e.g., smarter test generation, adaptive/self-healing approaches, and AI-enabled test execution where applicable) to reduce script fragility and speed up automation development. Create and maintain test plans, automation suites, and execution pipelines to run on-demand and on schedule; ensure results are observable via dashboards/logs/reports and are usable for release decisions. Execute and monitor automated test runs across builds; analyze failures to distinguish product defects vs. test issues , improve stability, and keep the automation suite production-grade. Measure and communicate automation coverage, ROI, quality trends, and release risk ; continuously prioritize automation work based on defect trends and usage-critical paths. Collaborate with cross-functional and global stakeholders (developers, architects, product owners, system engineers) to improve testability and promote quality best practices throughout the lifecycle Job Requirements Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Computer Applications, Software Engineering, Automation, Electronic Engineering, or a related technical field. Familiarity with software quality control processes and a good understanding of web UI testing concepts. Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language such as C/C++, Python, Perl, or VBScript. Experience with Visual Studio, automated testing frameworks, MySQL or Oracle databases, and Linux commands is preferred. Fluent in spoken and written English. Strong initiative, fast learning ability, proactive attitude, and excellent team spirit. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. description: Your primary mission will be to design, build, and take to production Generative AI tools and Large Language Model (LLM) applications that assist our analytical modelers in their day-to-day work — AI co-pilots for code generation, automated model-documentation and validation generators, and monitoring agents. Own the technical design end to end, including model selection, prompting and orchestration strategy, retrieval design, tool integration, and evaluation criteria. Agentic & Retrieval Systems: Design agent architectures with clear tool boundaries, guardrails, and fallback behaviour. Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines over internal data, including chunking strategy, embedding selection, index design, hybrid search, and grounding/citation quality. Define how agents are evaluated for correctness, hallucination, and safety before release. Cloud Platform & Deployment Architecture: Design and operate highly available, multi-service AI workloads on Google Cloud Platform. Take ownership of the cloud architecture for AI applications — compute and serving patterns (Cloud Run, GKE), networking (VPC, private service access, egress controls), identity (IAM service accounts, least privilege), secrets (Secret Manager), storage and data services (GCS, BigQuery), and managed AI services (Vertex AI, Vertex Vector Search). Make deliberate trade-offs on scalability, latency, resilience, and cost. AI-Ops & LLMOps at Scale: Establish and mature AI-Ops/LLMOps pipelines covering the full lifecycle of Generative AI tools: automated deployment, model and prompt versioning, artifact and evaluation tracking, regression testing of prompts and agents, and continuous monitoring for quality, drift, latency, token cost, and hallucination mitigation. Build the reusable platform components that let other engineers ship GenAI safely without rebuilding foundations. CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code: Own CI/CD and infrastructure automation for AI services using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Cloud Build, Kubernetes manifests) and GitOps practices. Deliver reproducible, auditable, environment-parity deployments with automated testing, progressive rollout, and clean rollback paths. Containerization & Performance Engineering: Package and serve AI applications as containerized microservices (Docker/Kubernetes), tuning autoscaling, resource requests and limits, cold-start behaviour, concurrency, caching, and batch versus real-time serving patterns. Drive down inference cost and latency without compromising quality. Observability, Reliability & SRE: Instrument AI systems with structured logging, distributed tracing, metrics, alerting, and dashboards. Define SLIs/SLOs for AI services, run incident response and root-cause analysis, and design for graceful degradation when upstream model providers or quotas fail. Security, Governance & Model Risk: Ensure every AI solution meets Ford's data privacy, security, compliance, and model-risk standards. Implement guardrails for internal data usage, prompt-injection and data-leakage protection, PII handling, access control, and audit trails — and produce the documentation and evidence needed for governance and audit review. Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Provide technical direction across the AI engineering team: set coding, architecture, and evaluation standards; conduct design and code reviews; mentor engineers and modelers on GenAI engineering practice; and translate ambiguous business problems into scoped, sequenced technical roadmaps. Act as a trusted reviewer for peers and a bridge between analytics, platform, and risk stakeholders. User-Centric Collaboration: Partner closely with analytical modelers to understand their daily bottlenecks, data prep challenges, and coding workflows, and convert those pain points into measurable AI products. Define success metrics up front and validate impact after adoption. Skills & Knowledge LLM & GenAI Technologies: Strong hands-on experience with LLM orchestration and agent frameworks (e.g., Google ADK, MCP), prompt and context engineering, function/tool calling, and working with both commercial and open-source foundation models — including reasoning about model capability, context limits, latency, and cost. Cloud Platform (GCP): Strong hands-on experience designing and operating on Google Cloud Platform: Cloud Run, Cloud Build, GKE, GCS, BigQuery, Vertex AI, Vertex Vector Search, IAM, VPC networking, Secret Manager, and Artifact Registry. Comfortable contributing to cloud architecture decisions — service selection, networking topology, quota management, and cost optimization. AI-Ops / LLMOps: Working knowledge of tools and platforms for model deployment, prompt and model versioning, evaluation harnesses, tracing, and monitoring of LLM and GenAI outputs in production. Experience defining evaluation datasets, automated scoring, and quality gates for GenAI releases. DevOps, IaC & SRE Practices: Good proficiency in CI/CD tooling, GitOps, containerization (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and cloud-native monitoring, logging, and alerting. Vector Databases & Retrieval: Experience with vector search and embedding technologies (e.g., Vertex Vector Search, sentence transformers) and the retrieval patterns that sit on top of them — hybrid search, re-ranking, and grounded generation. Software Engineering: Strong hands-on Python engineering (5+ years), building APIs (FastAPI, Flask) that serve AI models to end users, with good typing, testing, packaging, and code-review practice. Enough full-stack understanding to integrate front-end, back-end, and AI services reliably. Security & Compliance: Familiarity with cloud security practices, identity and access management, secrets management, network policies, and compliance requirements in regulated environments. Analytics Workflow Understanding: Familiarity with the workflows of data scientists and modelers (data wrangling, feature engineering, model validation) so you can build tools that fit how they work.
